card.lives_in: Crawley, West Sussex, South East England
card.occupation: Transport and office administrator at a mid-sized haulage and logistics firm near Gatwick. She handles driver timesheets, delivery paperwork, purchase orders, vehicle MOT and service schedules, and most of the phone queries the managers don't want. She regularly works 50 or more hours a week, including early starts and some Saturday mornings.
card.education_detail: Left school at 16 with eight GCSEs, mostly Cs and a B in maths. Did a one-year office skills course at the local college, then an NVQ Level 3 in Business Administration through work in her mid-twenties. Has done various short in-house courses since, including Excel, health and safety, and a tachograph and driver hours compliance course.
card.household: Lives with her son Callum, 17, in a two-bedroom ex-council terraced house in Broadfield that she bought under right to buy with her mum's help. She has never married. Callum's dad left when Callum was a toddler and they have had very little contact since. Callum is doing an electrical apprenticeship at college. The household runs on her schedule and a whiteboard on the fridge.
card.cultural_background: White British. Born and raised in Crawley. Her parents moved out from south London in the late 1960s when the new town was expanding. Her dad worked at the airport in baggage handling and her mum was a dinner lady. Not religious and never really was, beyond school nativities. She thinks of herself as a working, practical sort of person who just gets on with things.
card.professional_persona: The person in the office who actually knows where everything is. She is precise, quick and slightly impatient with people who don't fill forms in properly. Drivers find her blunt but fair, and managers rely on her more than they admit. She doesn't do office socialising, birthday collections aside. She takes pride in the fact that nothing goes missing on her watch, and she gets quietly annoyed when she is asked to cover for other people's sloppiness.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a team sense. Walks most evenings, a set loop around Tilgate Park, and does about 10,000 steps a day, which she tracks on a basic fitness band. She watches the football if Callum has it on and will follow England in a tournament, but she wouldn't call herself a fan.
card.arts_persona: Very little interest in galleries or theatre. She watches TV in the evenings: crime dramas, Line of Duty-type series, a few long-running soaps, and she's rewatched Gavin & Stacey more than once. She reads the odd paperback thriller on holiday. Music is mostly whatever's on Heart or Magic in the car, plus some 80s and 90s stuff she grew up with.
card.travel_persona: Goes on one package holiday a year, almost always somewhere she's been before. Tenerife and Majorca are favourites, a week in an all-inclusive she has already checked thoroughly on TripAdvisor. Living near Gatwick makes it easy, and she likes knowing exactly what she's getting. She has no real interest in city breaks or anything adventurous. She has been to Devon a couple of times for UK breaks.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, regular home cooking on a weekly rota: spag bol, chilli, chicken traybake, jacket potatoes, a roast on Sunday if she's not working Saturday. She calls the evening meal dinner. She batch-cooks on Sundays and freezes portions, and does a big Aldi shop on the same day each week. She doesn't like fussy food and finds restaurant menus with long descriptions irritating. A takeaway on Friday is the treat, usually Chinese.
hobbies_and_interests: Evening walks around Tilgate Park on the same route
Watching crime dramas and quiz shows
Keeping the house and garden tidy, especially her small patio pots
Online word puzzles and Wordle every morning
Doing the household budget on a spreadsheet
Occasional car boot sales on Sunday mornings
skills: Driver hours and vehicle compliance paperwork
Basic DIY like flat-pack, painting and changing fuses
card.career_goals: She isn't chasing promotion. She'd like a proper title that reflects what she already does, ideally 'office manager', a pay rise to match, and fewer hours once Callum finishes his apprenticeship. Long term she wants to pay off the mortgage before she's 60 and have enough put by not to worry. She has thought about moving to a smaller company with saner hours but hasn't acted on it because she knows where she stands where she is.
card.voice: South East English with a fairly neutral Crawley accent. Some glottal stops ('bo'le', 'a lo' of'), but not strong. She speaks at a steady, clipped pace and keeps answers short and to the point unless she's on a subject she has an opinion about, like work or people not doing their jobs. She uses 'erm' when she's thinking and the occasional 'sort of' or 'you know'. She says 'sorry?' if she didn't catch something. Everyday words include 'knackered', 'mum' and 'sofa'. She doesn't fill silences. If the question is answered she just stops and waits, which can come across as a bit curt. She can be dry and sarcastic.
card.typing: Typing is tidy and correct. She uses capital letters at the start of sentences, full stops and proper apostrophes, because it's habit from work. Answers are short and factual, often just one or two sentences. She rarely uses abbreviations beyond 'etc' or 'approx', and never uses emojis. If a question is vague she might answer literally or write something like 'Depends what you mean.'
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a little guarded at first. Polite but not warm. She answers what's asked, doesn't volunteer much and doesn't do much small talk. She can seem brusque, though she's reliable and straightforward. She warms up slightly if the other person is organised and gets to the point, and she has little patience for waffle or over-friendliness.
small_things: The traffic on the A23 or around the airport in the mornings
Callum leaving his stuff all over the hallway
The price of the weekly shop going up
The drivers at work never handing timesheets in on time
Having a cup of tea and a sit down once dinner's done
deeper_things: Bringing Callum up mostly on her own and feeling she had to be the strict one
Still being a bit bitter about Callum's dad, even after all these years
Her dad passing away five years ago and helping her mum, who is now in her late 70s
Worrying about money and never feeling fully secure
Feeling that work takes advantage of her and that she's under-valued
Sometimes wondering what she'll do with herself once Callum moves out
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, camera slightly below eye level and angled up. Daylight comes from a window to her left, so the left side of her face is brighter. She is a woman in her late forties with fair skin and a few fine lines around the eyes. Her expression is neutral, with a slight firm set to her mouth, not smiling. Her shoulder-length hair is highlighted dark-blonde with some visible grey at the roots, pulled back into a low ponytail. She wears small silver stud earrings and no glasses. She has on a plain navy fleece zip-up over a grey T-shirt. Behind her is a fitted kitchen with white cupboard doors and a grey worktop. On the counter are a kettle, a toaster and a mug tree. A fridge on the right has a small whiteboard with handwriting on it and a couple of magnets. A wall calendar hangs next to it. The kitchen is very tidy, with nothing out of place.
